Andrew / team — attaching the technical summary and network diagram (network-diagrams-v2.pdf). Below is the extracted checklist for your security team to paste into Helios' allowlist tooling.

Summary (concise):
- Outbound IPs (control plane & telemetry): 34.210.112.45, 34.210.112.46, 34.210.112.47
- Model artifact fetch (blob storage endpoints): *.redwood-artifacts-us.redwood-inference.internal (resolves to the IPs above, we recommend allowing by FQDN + SNI)
- Ports: 443 (HTTPS/TLS) outbound required; 80 not used.
- Protocols: TLSv1.2+; we support TLS1.3.
- mTLS: Optional for customer proxy fronting private endpoint. If Helios wants mutual TLS we can provide client certs pinned to CN=redwood-inference-client and rotate on a quarterly cadence.
- DNS: allow outbound to closest authoritative resolver; our runtime does SRV queries for artifact discovery but standard A/AAAA lookups suffice.

Fallback behavior:
- If allowlist blocks control-plane telemetry: request latency will increase; SDKs have a 10s connect timeout and retries with exponential backoff (3 attempts) before surfacing an error to the app. No silent fallback to hosted models — requests will fail fast if network-level egress is blocked.
- If artifact fetches are blocked: model loads will fail and the runtime will return a clear 503 with retry-after header. We recommend allowing FQDN patterns to avoid transient IP changes during scale events.

Operational notes:
- We publish an operational IP change log to the shared Drive link below and will notify via the HubSpot deal webhook when changes occur.
- For higher assurance we can enable mTLS on a per-tenant basis and provide an attestation bundle (PKI chain + rotation policy).

Attachments: network-diagrams-v2.pdf; redwood-private-endpoint-checklist.docx

Regards,
David Kim
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
